direct_answer:
Aker BP states that it conducted a double materiality assessment (DMA) using a systematic, four-step process that maps impacts, risks and opportunities (IROs), their dependencies, and their connection to Aker BP’s own operations and value chain, considering activities, business relationships and geographies [Source 8] [Source 5]. The DMA covers both (i) impact materiality (inside-out: impacts on environment and society) and (ii) financial materiality (outside-in: financial risks and opportunities to the business model and performance), explicitly including reputational risk and dependencies on natural, human and social resources [Source 3]. IROs are assessed and prioritised using a severity × likelihood approach aligned with the company’s enterprise risk management methodology (consequence × probability), documented in the same tool as other company risks and handled together with them; special attention is given to dependencies between impacts and corresponding risks/opportunities [Source 3]. The process is described as structured and iterative: defining business context (activities, business model, value chain, stakeholders, boundaries), identifying actual/potential IROs using top-down and bottom-up approaches with internal/external stakeholder input and quantitative sources, assessing/prioritising against impact and financial criteria using a standardised rating system, and validating outcomes by management and the Board with ongoing monitoring/updates [Source 7].

Stakeholder engagement is described as open and proactive dialogue through multiple internal and external channels (e.g., public consultations for PDO impact assessments shared with “over 40 key stakeholders”, publication of impact assessments, and a whistleblowing channel), and Aker BP says it incorporates stakeholders’ perspectives and priorities into the DMA [Source 1]. For the 2024 DMA, Aker BP used in-depth interviews and workshops with internal management and subject matter experts, and notes that the process was based on interviews performed in the previous year involving owners, key suppliers, customers, NGOs and authorities [Source 1].

Sustainability matters identified as material from both an impact and a financial perspective (i.e., high impact and high financial relevance / “strategic and highest priority”) are: climate change, own workforce, pollution, business conduct, and resource use and circular economy [Source 5].
compliance_rationale: The passages provide a clear description that Aker BP performed a DMA covering both impact and financial materiality, including how IROs are identified, assessed (severity×likelihood), prioritised, integrated into ERM, and validated by management/Board, and they identify the topics assessed as material in both dimensions [Source 3] [Source 7] [Source 5]. Stakeholder engagement channels and stakeholder groups considered are described, and Aker BP states stakeholder perspectives are included in the DMA [Source 1]. However, the evidence provided does not specify the exact qualitative/quantitative thresholds or scoring cut-offs used to determine materiality, nor does it list the full set of material IROs (Table 3 is referenced but not included in the retrieved passages) [Source 3] [Source 9].
disclosure_gaps: Specific qualitative and/or quantitative thresholds (e.g., scoring cut-offs) used to determine which impacts/risks/opportunities and sustainability matters are material are not provided in the retrieved passages [Source 3] [Source 7].

A complete list of the identified material impacts, risks and opportunities (IROs) is referenced (Table 3) but not included in the retrieved passages, so the detailed IRO outcomes cannot be confirmed here [Source 9].

How impact materiality severity dimensions (scale, scope, irremediable character) were operationalised is not evidenced in the retrieved passages (only severity×likelihood is described at a high level) [Source 3].
How financial materiality magnitude was operationalised (e.g., what constitutes ‘material financial effects’) is not evidenced in the retrieved passages [Source 3] [Source 9].

Explicit description of how upstream vs downstream value-chain impacts/risks were systematically assessed across all topics (beyond high-level statements and some topic-specific notes) is limited in the retrieved passages [Source 5] [Source 13] [Source 14].
key_findings: Aker BP revised its DMA in 2024 based on new information, implementation guidance and a draft oil & gas sector standard, and mapped IROs, dependencies and value-chain connections using a four-step process [Source 8].
DMA covers both impact (inside-out) and financial (outside-in) materiality, including reputational risk and dependencies on natural, human and social resources [Source 3].
IROs are assessed/prioritised using severity×likelihood aligned with the enterprise risk management approach and documented/managed in the same tool as other company risks [Source 3].

Stakeholder engagement informs the DMA via multiple channels (PDO public consultations, publishing impact assessments, whistleblowing channel) and via interviews/workshops; stakeholder groups include owners, suppliers, customers, NGOs and authorities [Source 1].
Topics identified as material from both impact and financial perspectives are climate change, own workforce, pollution, business conduct, and resource use and circular economy [Source 5].
